surface_mechanism_description: The growth of chromium oxide layers involves self-limiting chemisorption of a metal halide (CrO2Cl2) and water vapor under limiting surface coverage conditions. The process on hydroxylated surfaces can be run according to the schemes: –OH) + CrO2Cl2 → –O–)CrO2Cl2 + HCl, and |–O–)mCrO2Cl2 → |–O–)mCrO2Cl2 + HCl. Repeating these reactions many times and intermittently removing the reaction products and excess reagents allows for the growth of an oxide layer of predetermined thickness.
